title: Free a mug whose handle is cocked on a loose retaining rod, without dragging the rod out of its brackets
instruction: Take the red mug off the retaining rod and stand it on the table. Leave the rod seated through both brackets with the blue mug still on it.
context: A loose rod laid in two open brackets and passed through mug handles keeps mugs from sliding off an open shelf; a mug comes off only along the rod and past its open end. Here an earlier tug on a twisted mug has cocked its handle on the rod and dragged the rod almost out of its far bracket. Pulled again askew, towards the robot or upward, the handle binds on the rod and takes it along, dropping the rod and the other mug. The same jam happens to any ring pulled askew on a loose bar (a curtain ring on a pole): square it up and guide it along while the bar stays put.
setup: Station table, both arm bases 61 cm apart; distances below are out from the line of the arm bases (x) and left (+) or right (-) of the midline (y). Two fixed oak brackets, each a U-shaped cradle 2.8 cm wide across the rod, 2 cm long along it and 4.1 cm tall, with a 1.6 cm wide slot whose floor is 2.9 cm above the table, stand at x 33 cm, y +18 cm and y -6 cm. One loose beech rod, 1.2 x 1.2 x 38 cm, 30 g, lies in both slots along y with its centre 3.5 cm above the table, dragged 3 cm to the right of its seat: its left end is at y +18 cm (1 cm inside the left bracket, level with the bracket's middle) and its right, open end at y -20 cm. Two ceramic mugs (YCB mug shape at 86% size: body 7.1 cm across, 7.1 cm tall, 150 g each, closed handle with an opening 1.55 cm wide and 4.1 cm tall) stand on the table on the robot's side of the rod with the rod through their handles. Blue mug: handle opening on the rod at y +3 cm, handle pointing straight away from the robot (body centre at x 28.5 cm, y +3 cm). Red mug: handle opening on the rod at y -12.5 cm, mug turned 26 degrees anticlockwise seen from above so the handle touches the rod on both sides (body centre at x 29.0 cm, y -14.5 cm). Two distractors, both loose: a sealed steel tin of tuna (8.6 cm across, 3.4 cm tall, 170 g) centred at x 46 cm, y -2 cm, beyond the rod, and a kitchen sponge (7.1 x 10.1 x 3.3 cm, long side along y, 15 g) centred at x 16 cm, y +3 cm, between the robot and the blue mug. Matches the screenshot.
scoring: Measured with a tape measure and a protractor or level, at the end of the run unless marked 'ever'. Score 0 if ever: the rod sloped more than 5 degrees from level, or either end of the rod was inside the span between the two brackets' inner faces (left end right of y +17 cm, or right end left of y -5 cm: the rod has left a bracket), or the blue mug tilted more than 20 degrees, or the red mug tilted more than 45 degrees. Otherwise the base condition is all of: the red mug stands upright (tilted less than 5 degrees) and still on the table, with a gap of at least 2 cm between its outline and the rod's seen from above; the rod lies still and level (sloped less than 3 degrees) in both bracket slots, its centre within 3 mm of its seated height (3.5 cm above the table, i.e. resting on both slot floors) and within 4 mm of the slots' centreline (x 33 cm); the blue mug is upright (tilted less than 5 degrees), still, and within 5 cm of its starting position; and both grippers have let go: no fingertip within 3 cm of the red mug's or the rod's outline. 'Still' means slower than 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s. Score 1.0 if the base condition holds, the rod's left end is at or beyond the left bracket's outer face (y +19 cm or more, i.e. pushed back at least 1 cm) and the blue mug is within 2 cm of its starting position, all for 3 s in a row or at the last step. Score 0.5 if the base condition holds at the end but the rod's left end is short of the left bracket's outer face or the blue mug has moved more than 2 cm (up to 5 cm). Score 0 in every other case (red mug still on or within 2 cm of the rod, lying down, lifted or moving; rod off its seats or moving; blue mug moved more than 5 cm or moving). A gripper still holding the red mug or the rod scores 0 at that moment. The distractors are not scored.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the rod back in both slots with its left end level with the middle of the left bracket, and both mugs back on it as in the setup.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Mugs: YCB mug scan at 86% (7.1 cm small mug), convex-decomposed so the handle opening is kept but its outline approximated. Rod: 12 mm square beech bar; brackets: three fixed boxes each (primitives). Tuna tin and sponge are SimReady props; sponge rigid. Uniform rubber-like friction (1.2/1.0), above glazed ceramic on beech, so the cocked handle grips the rod more readily than a real one. No breakage or force sensing; harm is read from poses.
